searchText: Are there L2 standards? There are many L2 implementations and deployed systems but they generally don't talk to each other. Perhaps we should have standards? Even in that case, still need liquidity providers, but interoperability gets much more straightforward. I imagine solutions such as starkware are effectively standards. Are there more examples? Then we'll need adaptors for inter-standard interoperability There are bridging solutions in the works, here is one: https://connext.network/ also I use zapper which looks to be adding it: https://zapper.fi/bridge also someone has thrown up an implementation of it, not sure if you can trust it or not https://www.xpollinate.io/ but enabled polygon <-> xdai <-> BSC at the moment, not really sure if this is the appropriate channel for this, probably off topic, feel like there should be a group for this. Zapper bridge I didn't know. Thanks. these are inter-chain interoperability bridges. I am talking about between different eth L2s say I want to send eth from account on deversifi to my account on loopring. can't do it now. But if there was an adaptor .. I could do that. Even swapping could be enabled if enough liquidity was present in an AMM-fashion. In order to build the adaptor, we will need standards first. I don't think it makes much sense to develop standards in this still very emergent field with plenty of unknowns. Let things crystallize for a bit, and then see what's what. it's fair point. But we are getting there I think faster than we can imagine. It will soon be a spaghetti of useless L2s connext will allow this they are an adapter that connect two stovepipe implementations. For every new L2 out there, they'll need at least some glue code to make the adapter work. It's not a sustainable solution long term. Can we have a channel for L2 research? <@!203220829473996800> or ETH2 standards <#829412277782315008> > 1. inclusion delay reward removed, with only attestations included in the next block being counted Not quite. Rather, the inclusion delay reward is being simplified; there's now rewards for being "very timely" (within 1 slot) and "timely" (within 5 slots). There's no more `1/delay` reward > 2. proportion of total per-epoch reward allocated to block proposer increased from 1/32 to 1/8 That sounds right. I think it was intended to be 1/8 all along actually 😆 > 3. overall per-epoch max issuance unchanged, so the source/target/head rewards will change to keep this invariant correct Well, technically, issuance is increased very slightly, because before there were some math errors that caused the actual maximum reward to be slightly *less* than the base-reward-based amount And Altair fixes those errors

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content:
> 1. inclusion delay reward removed, with only attestations included in the next block being counted

Not quite. Rather, the inclusion delay reward is being simplified; there's now rewards for being "very timely" (within 1 slot) and "timely" (within 5 slots). There's no more `1/delay` reward

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content:
> 2. proportion of total per-epoch reward allocated to block proposer increased from 1/32 to 1/8

That sounds right. I think it was intended to be 1/8 all along actually 😆
